name: Human
title: Human Atlas
blurb: Adult human anatomy — every bone, the major muscles, organs, vessels and nerves.

parts.name: Frontal Bone
parts.d: The bone of the forehead. It forms the front of the cranial vault, the roofs of both eye sockets and contains the frontal sinuses just above the nose.
parts.fn: Shields the frontal lobes of the brain, gives the forehead its shape and anchors the scalp muscles that raise the eyebrows.
parts.kid: Your forehead is one big curved bone — a crash helmet for the thinking part of your brain.

meta.Articulates with: Parietals, sphenoid, ethmoid, nasals, maxillae, zygomatics, lacrimals

parts.name: Parietal Bone
parts.d: One of a pair of large curved plates that make up the roof and upper sides of the skull. The two meet along the sagittal suture on top of the head.
parts.fn: Protects the parietal lobes, which handle touch, spatial awareness and body position.
parts.kid: The two bones on top of your head fit together like puzzle pieces. In babies they are still apart — that's the soft spot!

meta.Articulates with: Opposite parietal, frontal, occipital, temporal, sphenoid

parts.name: Occipital Bone
parts.d: The bone at the back and base of the skull. It contains the foramen magnum, the large opening through which the brainstem becomes the spinal cord.
parts.fn: Protects the visual cortex and cerebellum, and its two occipital condyles rest on the atlas (C1) to form the joint that lets you nod.
parts.kid: The bump at the back of your head is part of this bone. The big hole underneath lets your brain connect to your spinal cord.

parts.name: Temporal Bone
parts.d: Forms the lower side of the skull around the ear. It houses the middle and inner ear and has the mastoid process — the bump you can feel behind your earlobe.
parts.fn: Contains the organs of hearing and balance, forms the socket for the jaw joint and anchors neck muscles such as the sternocleidomastoid.
parts.kid: The bones around your ears hold the tiniest parts of your hearing system, deep inside where they are safe.

parts.name: Sphenoid Bone
parts.d: A butterfly-shaped bone in the middle of the skull base. Only its greater wings show at the temples; its body holds the sella turcica, the saddle that cradles the pituitary gland.
parts.fn: Links the cranial and facial skeleton, forms part of each eye socket and gives passage to the optic nerves and major cranial vessels.
parts.kid: Hidden in the middle of your head is a bone shaped like a butterfly. It holds a tiny gland that controls how you grow.

meta.Articulates with: All other cranial bones, plus vomer, zygomatics, palatines

parts.name: Ethmoid Bone
parts.d: A light, spongy bone between the eye sockets. Its perforated cribriform plate lets the olfactory nerves pass from the nose to the brain.
parts.fn: Forms the roof of the nasal cavity, part of the nasal septum and the inner walls of the orbits; its air cells lighten the skull.
parts.kid: Smell signals travel through tiny holes in this bone to reach your brain.

meta.Articulates with: Frontal, sphenoid, nasals, maxillae, lacrimals, palatines, vomer

parts.name: Maxilla
parts.d: The upper jaw bone. The two maxillae meet in the midline to hold the upper teeth, form most of the hard palate and the floor of each eye socket, and contain the large maxillary sinuses.
parts.fn: Holds the upper teeth, separates the mouth from the nose and transmits chewing forces up into the skull.
parts.kid: Your top teeth are rooted in this bone. It also makes the roof of your mouth.

meta.Articulates with: Frontal, nasal, zygomatic, lacrimal, palatine, vomer, ethmoid, opposite maxilla

parts.name: Zygomatic Bone
parts.d: The cheekbone. It forms the prominence of the cheek and the outer rim of the eye socket, and bridges back to the temporal bone as the zygomatic arch.
parts.fn: Protects the eye from the side, shapes the face and anchors the masseter, the main chewing muscle.
parts.kid: Touch the hard bump under your eye — that's your cheekbone.

parts.name: Nasal Bone
parts.d: A small oblong bone; the pair forms the bony bridge of the nose. The rest of the nose is shaped by cartilage.
parts.fn: Supports the upper nose and protects the nasal cavity. It is the most commonly fractured bone of the face.
parts.kid: The hard top part of your nose is made of two tiny bones — the floppy tip is cartilage.

parts.name: Lacrimal Bone
parts.d: The smallest facial bone, a thin plate in the inner wall of the eye socket about the size of a fingernail.
parts.fn: Contains the groove for the tear sac and the canal that drains tears into the nose — which is why crying makes your nose run.
parts.kid: This bone is smaller than your fingernail and helps drain your tears into your nose.

meta.Articulates with: Frontal, ethmoid, maxilla, inferior nasal concha

parts.name: Palatine Bone
parts.d: An L-shaped bone at the back of the nasal cavity. Its horizontal plate forms the back third of the hard palate.
parts.fn: Completes the roof of the mouth and the floor and side walls of the nasal cavity.
parts.kid: Run your tongue to the back of the roof of your mouth — that hard part is the palatine bone.

meta.Articulates with: Maxilla, sphenoid, ethmoid, vomer, inferior nasal concha

parts.name: Inferior Nasal Concha
parts.d: A scroll-like bone projecting from the side wall of each nasal cavity.
parts.fn: Swirls inhaled air over moist lining so it is warmed, humidified and filtered before it reaches the lungs.
parts.kid: Inside your nose are curly bones that warm up air before you breathe it in.

parts.name: Vomer
parts.d: A thin, ploughshare-shaped bone that forms the lower back part of the nasal septum.
parts.fn: Divides the nasal cavity into left and right passages together with the septal cartilage.
parts.kid: A thin bone wall splits your nose into two tunnels.

parts.name: Mandible
parts.d: The lower jaw — the largest and strongest bone of the face and the only skull bone that moves freely.
parts.fn: Holds the lower teeth and moves at the temporomandibular joints for chewing, biting, speaking and yawning.
parts.kid: Your jaw is the only bone in your head that can move. Try opening and closing your mouth!

parts.name: Hyoid Bone
parts.d: A horseshoe-shaped bone in the front of the neck, just above the larynx. It is the only bone in the body that does not touch another bone.
parts.fn: Anchors the tongue and the muscles of the floor of the mouth, and helps raise the larynx during swallowing and speech.
parts.kid: This floating bone in your neck isn't attached to any other bone — it's held up by muscles like a hammock.

parts.name: Malleus
parts.d: The hammer: the first and largest of the three middle-ear bones, attached to the eardrum.
parts.fn: Picks up eardrum vibrations and passes them to the incus.

parts.name: Incus
parts.d: The anvil: the middle ossicle, linking the malleus to the stapes.
parts.fn: Relays and amplifies sound vibrations across the middle ear.

parts.name: Stapes
parts.d: The stirrup: at about 3 mm long it is the smallest bone in the body. Its footplate sits in the oval window of the inner ear.
parts.fn: Pushes sound vibrations into the fluid of the cochlea, completing the lever system that amplifies sound about twentyfold.

parts.name: Atlas (C1)
parts.d: The first cervical vertebra, a ring of bone with no body that carries the skull on two kidney-shaped facets.
parts.fn: Supports the head and forms the atlanto-occipital joint, which lets you nod 'yes'.
parts.kid: Your neck has 7 bones — the same number as a giraffe's!

parts.name: Axis (C2)
parts.d: The second cervical vertebra. Its tooth-like dens projects up through the ring of the atlas and acts as a pivot.
parts.fn: The atlas and skull rotate around the dens — the joint that lets you shake your head 'no'.
parts.kid: Your neck has 7 bones — the same number as a giraffe's!

parts.name: Cervical Vertebra C3
parts.d: The third cervical vertebra. Cervical vertebrae are small and light, with a hole in each transverse process for the vertebral artery.
parts.fn: Supports and moves the head and neck while protecting the cervical spinal cord and the vertebral arteries that run through its transverse foramina.
parts.kid: Your neck has 7 bones — the same number as a giraffe's!

parts.name: Vertebra Prominens (C7)
parts.d: The seventh cervical vertebra, with a long spinous process you can feel as the bump at the base of the neck.
parts.fn: Anchors the nuchal ligament and neck and back muscles; a surface landmark for counting vertebrae.

parts.name: Thoracic Vertebra T1
parts.d: The first thoracic vertebra. Thoracic vertebrae have facets on their bodies and transverse processes for the ribs and long, downward-sloping spinous processes.
parts.fn: Articulates with a pair of ribs to form the back of the rib cage, protects the thoracic spinal cord and allows twisting of the upper trunk.
parts.kid: Each of these 12 back bones holds on to a pair of ribs.

parts.name: Lumbar Vertebra L1
parts.d: The first lumbar vertebra. Lumbar vertebrae have the largest bodies in the spine because they bear the most weight.
parts.fn: Carries most of the body's weight above the pelvis and allows bending forwards and backwards; protects the cauda equina nerve roots.
parts.kid: These 5 big bones in your lower back carry the weight of your whole upper body.

parts.name: Sacrum
parts.d: A large triangular bone formed by five fused vertebrae (S1–S5) at the base of the spine, wedged between the two hip bones.
parts.fn: Transfers the weight of the upper body to the pelvis through the sacroiliac joints and forms the back wall of the pelvic cavity.
parts.kid: Five bones grow together into one strong triangle that connects your spine to your hips.

parts.name: Coccyx
parts.d: The tailbone: three to five small fused vertebrae at the very bottom of the spine.
parts.fn: An attachment point for pelvic-floor muscles, tendons and ligaments, and it helps bear weight when you sit leaning back.
parts.kid: Your tailbone is what's left of a tail our distant ancestors had.

parts.name: Intervertebral Disc C2–C3
parts.d: The fibrocartilage cushion between C2 and C3: a tough outer ring (annulus fibrosus) around a gel-like core (nucleus pulposus).
parts.fn: Absorbs shock, spreads load evenly across the vertebrae and allows the spine to bend and twist.
parts.kid: Squishy discs between your back bones work like shock absorbers when you jump.

parts.name: Sternum
parts.d: The breastbone: a flat bone in the centre of the chest made of the manubrium, body and xiphoid process.
parts.fn: Forms the front of the rib cage, protects the heart, lungs and great vessels, and anchors the clavicles and first seven pairs of ribs. Its marrow makes blood cells throughout life.
parts.kid: The flat bone in the middle of your chest is a shield for your heart.

parts.name: Rib 1
parts.d: The first rib — a true rib. True ribs (1–7) attach directly to the sternum through their own costal cartilage.
parts.fn: The shortest, flattest and most curved rib; it frames the top of the chest where major vessels and nerves pass to the arm.
parts.kid: You have 12 pairs of ribs — 24 bones that make a cage to protect your heart and lungs.

parts.name: Costal Cartilage 1
parts.d: The bar of hyaline cartilage that extends rib 1 to the sternum.
parts.fn: Gives the rib cage the springiness it needs to expand when you inhale and to absorb blows to the chest.
parts.kid: The bendy ends of your ribs let your chest spring outwards when you breathe in.

parts.name: Clavicle
parts.d: The collarbone: an S-shaped strut running from the sternum to the acromion of the scapula.
parts.fn: Holds the arm away from the body so it can swing freely, and transmits force from the arm to the trunk. It is the only bony link between the arm and the torso.

parts.name: Scapula
parts.d: The shoulder blade: a flat, triangular bone on the upper back. Its ridge (the spine) ends in the acromion, the point of the shoulder, and its shallow glenoid cavity forms the socket of the shoulder joint.

parts.kid: The pointy part of your elbow is the top of the ulna.

parts.name: Radius

parts.fn: Rotates around the ulna to turn the palm up (supination) and down (pronation). Its lower end is the most commonly broken bone in adults.
parts.kid: Twist your hand palm up, then palm down — the radius is rolling over the ulna.

parts.name: Hip Bone
parts.d: Also called the os coxae or innominate bone: the ilium, ischium and pubis fuse during the teenage years to form one large bone on each side of the pelvis.
parts.fn: Transfers body weight from the spine to the legs, protects the pelvic organs and anchors the powerful hip and trunk muscles. Its cup, the acetabulum, is the socket of the hip joint.

parts.fn: Holds the pelvic ring together while allowing slight movement; it loosens during pregnancy to widen the birth canal.
parts.kid: The front of your hips is joined by a tough cushion of cartilage.

parts.name: Femur
parts.d: The thigh bone — the longest, heaviest and strongest bone in the body, about a quarter of your height.
parts.fn: Carries the body's weight from the hip to the knee and anchors the thigh muscles used for standing, walking and running. Its marrow is a major site of blood-cell production in children.
parts.kid: Your thigh bone is the longest bone in your body — and stronger than concrete for its weight!

parts.name: Patella
parts.d: The kneecap: the largest sesamoid bone in the body, embedded in the tendon of the quadriceps.
parts.fn: Protects the front of the knee and acts like a pulley, increasing the leverage of the quadriceps when you straighten your leg.
parts.kid: Babies are born with kneecaps made of soft cartilage that only turn to bone at around 3 to 5 years old.

parts.name: Tibia
parts.d: The shinbone: the larger, weight-bearing bone of the lower leg. Its front edge lies just under the skin, which is why knocks to the shin hurt so much.
parts.fn: Transmits body weight from the knee to the ankle. Its lower end forms the inner ankle bump (medial malleolus).
parts.kid: Your shinbone carries your weight down to your feet.

parts.name: Fibula
parts.d: The slender outer bone of the lower leg. It carries little weight; its lower end forms the outer ankle bump (lateral malleolus).
parts.fn: Stabilises the ankle joint and anchors the muscles that turn the foot outwards. Surgeons can remove part of it to rebuild a jaw without losing the ability to walk.
parts.kid: The thin bone on the outside of your leg helps keep your ankle steady.

parts.name: Medial Meniscus
parts.d: A C-shaped wedge of fibrocartilage on the inner half of the tibial plateau. It is firmly attached to the joint capsule, so it is torn more often than the lateral meniscus.
parts.fn: Deepens the knee socket, spreads load across the joint and absorbs shock.
parts.kid: Rubbery crescents in your knee cushion every step.

parts.name: Lateral Meniscus
parts.d: A nearly circular fibrocartilage ring on the outer half of the tibial plateau, more mobile than its medial partner.
parts.fn: Cushions and stabilises the lateral side of the knee.
parts.kid: Each knee has two cushions shaped like the letter C.

meta.Action: Lifts the shoulder blade and tilts the neck

parts.kid: Back muscles keep you standing tall.

parts.name: Latissimus Dorsi

parts.fn: Pulls the arm down and back — the swimming, rowing and pull-up muscle.

parts.name: Rhomboid Major

parts.name: Rhomboid Minor

parts.name: Supraspinatus

meta.Action: Starts lifting the arm out to the side

parts.name: Infraspinatus

meta.Action: Rotates the arm outwards

parts.name: Subscapularis

parts.fn: Rotates the arm inwards
parts.kid: Your shoulder is the most movable joint in your body, thanks to these muscles.

meta.Action: Rotates the arm inwards

parts.name: Teres Minor

parts.fn: Rotates the arm outwards
parts.kid: Your shoulder is the most movable joint in your body, thanks to these muscles.

meta.Action: Rotates the arm outwards

parts.name: Teres Major

parts.fn: Pulls the arm down and rotates it inwards
parts.kid: Your shoulder is the most movable joint in your body, thanks to these muscles.

meta.Insertion: Medial lip of the intertubercular groove
meta.Action: Pulls the arm down and rotates it inwards

parts.name: Deltoid
parts.d: The thick triangular muscle that caps the shoulder, with front, middle and back fibres.
parts.fn: Lifts the arm forwards, sideways and backwards
parts.kid: Your shoulder is the most movable joint in your body, thanks to these muscles.

meta.Origin: Lateral clavicle, acromion and spine of the scapula
meta.Action: Lifts the arm forwards, sideways and backwards

parts.name: Pectoralis Major

meta.Insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular groove of the humerus
meta.Action: Pulls the arm forwards and across the chest and rotates it inwards

parts.name: Pectoralis Minor
parts.d: A thin triangular muscle underneath the pectoralis major.
parts.fn: Pulls the shoulder blade forwards and down
parts.kid: Chest muscles help you push, hug and throw.

meta.Action: Pulls the shoulder blade forwards and down

parts.name: Serratus Anterior
parts.d: A saw-toothed muscle on the side of the chest.

meta.Insertion: Medial border of the scapula (front surface)
meta.Action: Holds the shoulder blade against the ribs and swings it forwards — the punching muscle

parts.name: Intercostal Muscles
parts.d: Three thin layers of muscle (external, internal and innermost) filling the spaces between the ribs.
parts.fn: Raise and lower the ribs during breathing
parts.kid: These muscles between your ribs help your chest get bigger when you breathe in.

meta.Insertion: Upper border of the rib below
meta.Action: Raise and lower the ribs during breathing

parts.name: Rectus Abdominis
parts.d: The long, strap-like 'six-pack' muscle down the front of the abdomen, divided into blocks by three or four tendinous intersections.
parts.fn: Bends the trunk forwards and supports the abdominal wall
parts.kid: Your tummy muscles protect your organs and help you sit up.

meta.Action: Bends the trunk forwards and supports the abdominal wall

parts.name: External Oblique
parts.d: The largest and outermost of the flat abdominal muscles, its fibres running down and forwards like hands in front pockets.
parts.fn: Twists and bends the trunk and compresses the abdomen
parts.kid: Your tummy muscles protect your organs and help you sit up.

meta.Insertion: Linea alba, pubic tubercle and iliac crest
meta.Action: Twists and bends the trunk and compresses the abdomen

parts.name: Internal Oblique
parts.d: The middle layer of the abdominal wall, its fibres at right angles to the external oblique.
parts.fn: Twists the trunk to the same side and compresses the abdomen
parts.kid: Your tummy muscles protect your organs and help you sit up.

meta.Origin: Thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, inguinal ligament
meta.Insertion: Lower ribs, linea alba and pubis
meta.Action: Twists the trunk to the same side and compresses the abdomen

parts.name: Transversus Abdominis
parts.d: The deepest abdominal muscle, with horizontal fibres.
parts.fn: Squeezes the abdomen like a corset, stabilising the spine
parts.kid: Your tummy muscles protect your organs and help you sit up.

meta.Origin: Lower costal cartilages, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest
meta.Action: Squeezes the abdomen like a corset, stabilising the spine

parts.name: Erector Spinae
parts.d: Three columns of muscle — iliocostalis, longissimus and spinalis — running up either side of the spine.
parts.fn: Straightens and arches the back and holds the spine upright
parts.kid: Back muscles keep you standing tall.

meta.Origin: Sacrum, iliac crest and spines of the lumbar vertebrae

meta.Action: Straightens and arches the back and holds the spine upright
meta.Nerve: Dorsal rami of the spinal nerves

parts.name: Quadratus Lumborum
parts.d: A deep, four-sided muscle of the lower back wall — a frequent source of lower back pain.
parts.fn: Hitches the hip and bends the trunk sideways
parts.kid: Back muscles keep you standing tall.

meta.Insertion: Rib 12 and the lumbar transverse processes
meta.Action: Hitches the hip and bends the trunk sideways

parts.name: Psoas Major
parts.d: A long, thick muscle beside the lumbar spine that joins the iliacus to form the iliopsoas, the strongest hip flexor.
parts.fn: Bends the hip (lifts the thigh) and bends the trunk forwards
parts.kid: Your bottom muscle, the gluteus maximus, is the biggest muscle in your body.

meta.Origin: Bodies and transverse processes of T12–L5
meta.Action: Bends the hip (lifts the thigh) and bends the trunk forwards

parts.name: Iliacus
parts.d: A fan-shaped muscle filling the inner bowl of the ilium.
parts.fn: Bends the hip
parts.kid: Your bottom muscle, the gluteus maximus, is the biggest muscle in your body.

meta.Origin: Iliac fossa of the hip bone
meta.Action: Bends the hip

parts.name: Gluteus Maximus
parts.d: The largest muscle in the body, forming the shape of the buttock.
parts.fn: Straightens the hip powerfully — climbing, running, standing up
parts.kid: Your bottom muscle, the gluteus maximus, is the biggest muscle in your body.

meta.Insertion: Iliotibial tract and gluteal tuberosity of the femur
meta.Action: Straightens the hip powerfully — climbing, running, standing up

parts.name: Gluteus Medius
parts.d: A fan-shaped muscle on the upper outer hip, partly under the gluteus maximus.
parts.fn: Lifts the leg sideways and keeps the pelvis level when you walk
parts.kid: Your bottom muscle, the gluteus maximus, is the biggest muscle in your body.

meta.Action: Lifts the leg sideways and keeps the pelvis level when you walk

parts.name: Gluteus Minimus
parts.d: The smallest and deepest of the three gluteal muscles.
parts.fn: Lifts the leg sideways and rotates the thigh inwards
parts.kid: Your bottom muscle, the gluteus maximus, is the biggest muscle in your body.

meta.Origin: Outer surface of the ilium, below gluteus medius
meta.Action: Lifts the leg sideways and rotates the thigh inwards

parts.name: Tensor Fasciae Latae
parts.d: A short muscle at the front edge of the hip, enclosed in the fascia lata.
parts.fn: Tightens the iliotibial band and helps lift and turn the thigh inwards
parts.kid: Your bottom muscle, the gluteus maximus, is the biggest muscle in your body.

meta.Action: Tightens the iliotibial band and helps lift and turn the thigh inwards

parts.name: Iliotibial Tract
parts.d: A long, thick band of fascia running down the outside of the thigh from the hip to the tibia.
parts.fn: Transmits the pull of the gluteus maximus and tensor fasciae latae to the knee and steadies it; overuse causes 'IT band syndrome' in runners.
parts.kid: A tough strap down the outside of your thigh.

meta.To: Lateral condyle of the tibia (Gerdy's tubercle)

parts.name: Biceps Brachii
parts.d: The two-headed muscle on the front of the upper arm.
parts.fn: Bends the elbow and turns the palm up
parts.kid: Bend your elbow and feel your biceps get fat and hard.

meta.Origin: Supraglenoid tubercle (long head) and coracoid process (short head)
meta.Action: Bends the elbow and turns the palm up

parts.name: Brachialis
parts.d: A broad muscle lying under the biceps.
parts.fn: Bends the elbow in any position — the main elbow flexor
parts.kid: Bend your elbow and feel your biceps get fat and hard.

meta.Insertion: Coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna
meta.Action: Bends the elbow in any position — the main elbow flexor

parts.name: Coracobrachialis
parts.d: A slender muscle in the upper inner arm; the musculocutaneous nerve pierces it.
parts.fn: Pulls the arm forwards and towards the body
parts.kid: Bend your elbow and feel your biceps get fat and hard.

meta.Action: Pulls the arm forwards and towards the body

parts.name: Triceps Brachii
parts.d: The three-headed muscle filling the back of the upper arm.
parts.fn: Straightens the elbow
parts.kid: Bend your elbow and feel your biceps get fat and hard.

meta.Origin: Infraglenoid tubercle (long head) and back of the humerus (lateral and medial heads)
meta.Action: Straightens the elbow

parts.name: Brachioradialis
parts.d: The muscle forming the outer bulge of the forearm below the elbow.
parts.fn: Bends the elbow with the thumb pointing up
parts.kid: Forearm muscles move your fingers using long tendons like puppet strings.

meta.Origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
meta.Action: Bends the elbow with the thumb pointing up

parts.name: Pronator Teres
parts.d: A short diagonal muscle across the upper front forearm.
parts.fn: Turns the palm down
parts.kid: Forearm muscles move your fingers using long tendons like puppet strings.

meta.Action: Turns the palm down

parts.name: Flexor Carpi Radialis
parts.d: A superficial forearm flexor whose tendon you can feel at the wrist.
parts.fn: Bends the wrist and tilts it towards the thumb
parts.kid: Forearm muscles move your fingers using long tendons like puppet strings.

meta.Action: Bends the wrist and tilts it towards the thumb

parts.name: Palmaris Longus
parts.d: A thin muscle with a long tendon — missing in about 1 in 7 people, and used by surgeons for tendon grafts.
parts.fn: Tightens the palm and helps bend the wrist
parts.kid: Press your thumb and little finger together — about 1 in 7 people won't see this tendon pop up.

meta.Action: Tightens the palm and helps bend the wrist

parts.name: Flexor Carpi Ulnaris
parts.d: The most medial superficial forearm flexor.
parts.fn: Bends the wrist and tilts it towards the little finger
parts.kid: Forearm muscles move your fingers using long tendons like puppet strings.

meta.Action: Bends the wrist and tilts it towards the little finger

parts.name: Flexor Digitorum Superficialis
parts.d: The largest superficial forearm muscle, sending four tendons through the carpal tunnel.
parts.fn: Bends the fingers at their middle joints
parts.kid: Forearm muscles move your fingers using long tendons like puppet strings.

meta.Origin: Medial epicondyle, coronoid process and radius
meta.Insertion: Middle phalanges of the four fingers
meta.Action: Bends the fingers at their middle joints

parts.name: Extensor Carpi Radialis Longus
parts.d: A long extensor on the thumb side of the forearm.
parts.fn: Straightens the wrist and tilts it towards the thumb
parts.kid: Forearm muscles move your fingers using long tendons like puppet strings.

meta.Action: Straightens the wrist and tilts it towards the thumb

parts.name: Extensor Digitorum
parts.d: The main finger extensor on the back of the forearm; its tendons show on the back of the hand.
parts.fn: Straightens the fingers and wrist
parts.kid: Forearm muscles move your fingers using long tendons like puppet strings.

meta.Insertion: Extensor hoods of the four fingers
meta.Action: Straightens the fingers and wrist

parts.name: Extensor Carpi Ulnaris
parts.d: The most medial extensor on the back of the forearm.
parts.fn: Straightens the wrist and tilts it towards the little finger
parts.kid: Forearm muscles move your fingers using long tendons like puppet strings.

meta.Origin: Lateral epicondyle and back of the ulna
meta.Action: Straightens the wrist and tilts it towards the little finger

parts.name: Thenar Muscles
parts.d: The fleshy pad at the base of the thumb: abductor pollicis brevis, flexor pollicis brevis and opponens pollicis.
parts.fn: Move the thumb across the palm to meet the fingers (opposition)
parts.kid: Tiny muscles in your hand let you write and pick up small things.

meta.Insertion: First metacarpal and proximal phalanx of the thumb
meta.Action: Move the thumb across the palm to meet the fingers (opposition)

parts.name: Hypothenar Muscles
parts.d: The padded edge of the palm under the little finger.
parts.fn: Move and cup the little finger
parts.kid: Tiny muscles in your hand let you write and pick up small things.

meta.Insertion: Fifth metacarpal and proximal phalanx of the little finger
meta.Action: Move and cup the little finger

parts.name: Sartorius
parts.d: The longest muscle in the body, a thin strap spiralling across the front of the thigh.
parts.fn: Bends, spreads and rotates the thigh outwards — the cross-legged tailor's position
parts.kid: The longest muscle in your body crosses your thigh like a sash.

meta.Action: Bends, spreads and rotates the thigh outwards — the cross-legged tailor's position

parts.name: Rectus Femoris
parts.d: The central muscle of the quadriceps, the only one that crosses the hip.
parts.fn: Straightens the knee and bends the hip — the kicking muscle
parts.kid: Thigh muscles are some of the strongest in your body.

meta.Origin: Anterior inferior iliac spine and above the acetabulum
meta.Insertion: Patella and, via the patellar ligament, the tibial tuberosity
meta.Action: Straightens the knee and bends the hip — the kicking muscle

parts.name: Vastus Lateralis
parts.d: The largest part of the quadriceps, on the outside of the thigh.
parts.fn: Straightens the knee
parts.kid: Thigh muscles are some of the strongest in your body.

meta.Origin: Greater trochanter and linea aspera of the femur
meta.Action: Straightens the knee

parts.name: Vastus Medialis
parts.d: The teardrop-shaped quadriceps muscle above the inner knee.
parts.fn: Straightens the knee and keeps the kneecap on track
parts.kid: Thigh muscles are some of the strongest in your body.

meta.Action: Straightens the knee and keeps the kneecap on track

parts.name: Vastus Intermedius
parts.d: The deepest quadriceps muscle, hidden under the rectus femoris.
parts.fn: Straightens the knee
parts.kid: Thigh muscles are some of the strongest in your body.

meta.Origin: Front and side of the femoral shaft
meta.Action: Straightens the knee

parts.name: Patellar Ligament
parts.d: The strong band continuing the quadriceps tendon below the kneecap to the tibial tuberosity.
parts.fn: Transmits the pull of the quadriceps to the tibia. Tapping it triggers the knee-jerk reflex.
parts.kid: When a doctor taps below your knee and your leg kicks, they're tapping this.

parts.name: Adductor Longus
parts.d: A triangular muscle on the inner thigh; strained in a 'groin pull'.
parts.fn: Pulls the thigh inwards
parts.kid: Thigh muscles are some of the strongest in your body.

meta.Action: Pulls the thigh inwards

parts.name: Adductor Brevis
parts.d: A short adductor lying behind the adductor longus.
parts.fn: Pulls the thigh inwards
parts.kid: Thigh muscles are some of the strongest in your body.

meta.Origin: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis
meta.Action: Pulls the thigh inwards

parts.name: Adductor Magnus
parts.d: The largest and deepest of the adductors, part adductor and part hamstring.
parts.fn: Pulls the thigh inwards and straightens the hip
parts.kid: Thigh muscles are some of the strongest in your body.

meta.Origin: Inferior pubic ramus, ischial ramus and ischial tuberosity
meta.Insertion: Linea aspera and adductor tubercle of the femur
meta.Action: Pulls the thigh inwards and straightens the hip

parts.name: Gracilis
parts.d: A long, slender strap along the inner thigh.
parts.fn: Pulls the thigh inwards and bends the knee
parts.kid: Thigh muscles are some of the strongest in your body.

meta.Origin: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis
meta.Action: Pulls the thigh inwards and bends the knee

parts.name: Pectineus
parts.d: A flat, quadrangular muscle at the top of the inner thigh.
parts.fn: Bends the hip and pulls the thigh inwards
parts.kid: Thigh muscles are some of the strongest in your body.

meta.Action: Bends the hip and pulls the thigh inwards

parts.name: Biceps Femoris
parts.d: The lateral hamstring muscle.
parts.fn: Bends the knee and straightens the hip
parts.kid: Hamstrings bend your knee — they're the muscles you stretch when you touch your toes.

meta.Origin: Ischial tuberosity (long head) and linea aspera (short head)
meta.Action: Bends the knee and straightens the hip

parts.name: Semitendinosus
parts.d: A medial hamstring with a long, cord-like lower tendon.
parts.fn: Bends the knee and straightens the hip
parts.kid: Thigh muscles are some of the strongest in your body.

meta.Action: Bends the knee and straightens the hip

parts.name: Semimembranosus
parts.d: The deepest medial hamstring, with a flat, membrane-like upper tendon.
parts.fn: Bends the knee and straightens the hip
parts.kid: Thigh muscles are some of the strongest in your body.

meta.Insertion: Back of the medial tibial condyle
meta.Action: Bends the knee and straightens the hip

parts.name: Gastrocnemius
parts.d: The two-headed calf muscle that gives the calf its shape.
parts.fn: Points the foot and bends the knee — rising on tiptoe, jumping
parts.kid: Calf muscles lift your whole body every time you stand on tiptoe.

meta.Origin: Medial and lateral condyles of the femur
meta.Action: Points the foot and bends the knee — rising on tiptoe, jumping

parts.name: Soleus
parts.d: A broad, flat calf muscle under the gastrocnemius — sometimes called the 'second heart' because it pumps venous blood up the leg.
parts.fn: Points the foot and keeps you from falling forwards while standing
parts.kid: Calf muscles lift your whole body every time you stand on tiptoe.

meta.Origin: Back of the upper tibia and fibula
meta.Action: Points the foot and keeps you from falling forwards while standing

parts.name: Achilles Tendon
parts.d: The thickest and strongest tendon in the body, joining the calf muscles to the heel bone.
parts.fn: Transfers the force of the calf to the heel for walking, running and jumping — it can bear several times body weight.
parts.kid: Named after the Greek hero Achilles, whose only weak spot was his heel.

parts.name: Tibialis Anterior
parts.d: The muscle along the front of the shin, just outside the tibia.
parts.fn: Lifts the foot (dorsiflexion) and turns the sole inwards
parts.kid: Calf muscles lift your whole body every time you stand on tiptoe.

meta.Origin: Upper lateral tibia and interosseous membrane
meta.Insertion: Medial cuneiform and base of the 1st metatarsal
meta.Action: Lifts the foot (dorsiflexion) and turns the sole inwards

parts.name: Extensor Digitorum Longus
parts.d: A long muscle beside tibialis anterior whose tendons fan out over the top of the foot.
parts.fn: Lifts the toes and the foot
parts.kid: Calf muscles lift your whole body every time you stand on tiptoe.

meta.Insertion: Middle and distal phalanges of toes 2–5
meta.Action: Lifts the toes and the foot

parts.name: Fibularis Longus
parts.d: The superficial muscle on the outer side of the leg; its tendon hooks behind the lateral malleolus and under the foot.
parts.fn: Turns the sole outwards and points the foot
parts.kid: Calf muscles lift your whole body every time you stand on tiptoe.

meta.Insertion: Medial cuneiform and base of the 1st metatarsal (under the foot)
meta.Action: Turns the sole outwards and points the foot

parts.name: Fibularis Brevis
parts.d: A shorter fibular muscle under the fibularis longus.
parts.fn: Turns the sole outwards
parts.kid: Calf muscles lift your whole body every time you stand on tiptoe.

meta.Action: Turns the sole outwards

parts.name: Tibialis Posterior
parts.d: The deepest calf muscle; weakness of it leads to flat feet.
parts.fn: Points the foot and supports the arch
parts.kid: Calf muscles lift your whole body every time you stand on tiptoe.

meta.Origin: Back of the tibia, fibula and interosseous membrane
meta.Action: Points the foot and supports the arch

parts.name: Plantar Muscles
parts.d: Four layers of small muscles in the sole of the foot, including flexor digitorum brevis and abductor hallucis.
parts.fn: Curl the toes and support the arches of the foot
parts.kid: Calf muscles lift your whole body every time you stand on tiptoe.

meta.Action: Curl the toes and support the arches of the foot

parts.name: Frontal Lobe
parts.d: The largest lobe, at the front of each hemisphere, ending at the central sulcus. It contains the primary motor cortex and, on the left side in most people, Broca's speech area.
parts.fn: Plans and controls voluntary movement, decision-making, attention, personality, impulse control and the production of speech.
parts.kid: This is your brain's control room — it helps you make plans and choices.

meta.Part: Cerebral cortex (grey matter) over white matter

parts.name: Parietal Lobe
parts.d: The lobe behind the central sulcus, at the top and back of each hemisphere. Its front strip is the primary somatosensory cortex.
parts.fn: Processes touch, temperature, pain and body position, and combines senses to judge space, size and direction.
parts.kid: It tells you where your body is — that's how you can touch your nose with your eyes closed.

meta.Part: Cerebral cortex (grey matter) over white matter

parts.name: Temporal Lobe
parts.d: The lobe on the side of each hemisphere, below the lateral sulcus, next to the ear. Its inner surface holds the hippocampus and amygdala.
parts.fn: Hearing, understanding language (Wernicke's area on the dominant side), recognising faces and objects, and forming new memories.
parts.kid: The part near your ears helps you hear and remember things.

meta.Part: Cerebral cortex (grey matter) over white matter

parts.name: Occipital Lobe
parts.d: The rearmost lobe of each hemisphere, sitting on the tentorium above the cerebellum.
parts.fn: Home of the primary visual cortex: it turns signals from the eyes into images, colour and motion.
parts.kid: You see with the back of your brain! Signals travel all the way from your eyes to here.

meta.Part: Cerebral cortex (grey matter) over white matter

parts.name: Cerebellum
parts.d: The 'little brain' tucked under the occipital lobes. Its tightly folded surface holds more than half of all the neurons in the brain.
parts.fn: Coordinates movement, balance, posture and timing, and fine-tunes skills learned by practice — from walking to playing an instrument.
parts.kid: This part helps you balance on a bike and catch a ball.

parts.name: Midbrain
parts.d: The top section of the brainstem, between the forebrain and the pons.
parts.fn: Relays visual and auditory reflexes, controls eye movement and pupil size, and contains the substantia nigra, whose dopamine neurons are lost in Parkinson's disease.
parts.kid: Deep in your brain, this part makes your eyes follow a moving ball.

parts.name: Pons
parts.d: The bulging bridge of the brainstem in front of the cerebellum.
parts.fn: Carries signals between the cerebrum and cerebellum, helps regulate breathing rhythm and sleep, and is the origin of several cranial nerves.
parts.kid: The pons is a bridge that carries messages across your brain.

parts.name: Medulla Oblongata
parts.d: The lowest part of the brainstem, continuous with the spinal cord at the foramen magnum.
parts.fn: Runs the automatic life-support centres: heart rate, blood pressure, breathing, swallowing, coughing and vomiting.
parts.kid: This part keeps your heart beating and your lungs breathing, even while you sleep.

parts.name: Thalamus
parts.d: A walnut-sized mass of grey matter deep in each hemisphere, on either side of the third ventricle.
parts.fn: The relay station for almost every sense (except smell) on its way to the cortex; also involved in alertness and sleep.
parts.kid: It's like a post office that sorts messages from your senses.

parts.name: Hypothalamus
parts.d: An almond-sized region below the thalamus that links the nervous system to the endocrine system through the pituitary gland.
parts.fn: Keeps the body in balance: body temperature, hunger, thirst, sleep cycles and the release of hormones that control growth, stress, reproduction and the thyroid.
parts.kid: It's your body's thermostat — it tells you when you're hungry, thirsty or too hot.

parts.name: Pituitary Gland
parts.d: The pea-sized 'master gland' hanging from the hypothalamus in a saddle of the sphenoid bone.
parts.fn: Releases growth hormone, TSH, ACTH, prolactin, FSH and LH, which in turn control the thyroid, adrenals and gonads; its back lobe releases ADH and oxytocin.
parts.kid: This tiny gland is the boss of many other glands in your body.

meta.Hormones: GH, TSH, ACTH, PRL, FSH, LH, ADH, oxytocin

parts.name: Pineal Gland
parts.d: A tiny pine-cone-shaped gland at the back of the third ventricle.
parts.fn: Secretes melatonin in darkness, helping to set the body's day–night (circadian) rhythm.
parts.kid: This gland makes a sleepy hormone when it gets dark.

parts.name: Corpus Callosum
parts.d: A thick band of about 200 million nerve fibres joining the left and right cerebral hemispheres.
parts.fn: Lets the two halves of the brain share information so they work as one.
parts.kid: It's a bridge of wires connecting the two halves of your brain.

parts.name: Hippocampus
parts.d: A seahorse-shaped structure curled inside the temporal lobe.
parts.fn: Converts short-term experiences into long-term memories and builds mental maps for navigation. It is one of the first regions affected in Alzheimer's disease.
parts.kid: Shaped like a seahorse, it helps you remember what you did today.

parts.name: Amygdala
parts.d: An almond-shaped cluster of neurons at the front of the hippocampus.
parts.fn: Detects threats and drives fear, anger and the fight-or-flight response; also tags memories with emotion.
parts.kid: This almond-shaped part makes you jump when something scares you.

parts.name: Olfactory Bulb
parts.d: The swelling at the front end of each olfactory tract (cranial nerve I), lying on the ethmoid bone.
parts.fn: Receives smell signals through the cribriform plate and passes them straight to the brain's emotion and memory areas — why smells trigger vivid memories.
parts.kid: Smells go straight from your nose to here.

parts.name: Optic Nerve
parts.d: Cranial nerve II: a cable of about a million nerve fibres running from the back of the eye to the optic chiasm, where half the fibres cross to the other side.
parts.fn: Carries visual information from the retina to the brain.
parts.kid: It's the cable that sends pictures from your eye to your brain.

parts.name: Spinal Cord
parts.d: The column of nerve tissue that runs from the brainstem down the vertebral canal to about the level of L1–L2 — around 45 cm long and as thick as a finger.
parts.fn: Carries motor commands down and sensory information up, and handles fast reflexes such as pulling your hand away from something hot on its own.
parts.kid: The spinal cord is the information highway between your brain and body.

parts.name: Cauda Equina
parts.d: The 'horse's tail': the bundle of lumbar and sacral nerve roots that continues down the vertebral canal below the end of the spinal cord.
parts.fn: Supplies the legs, bladder, bowel and genitals. Doctors take spinal fluid (lumbar puncture) from this level because there is no cord to injure.
parts.kid: Below the spinal cord, the nerves spread out like a horse's tail.

parts.name: Eyeball
parts.d: A sphere about 24 mm across made of three layers: the tough white sclera and clear cornea outside, the blood-rich choroid, and the light-sensing retina inside.
parts.fn: Focuses light onto the retina, whose 120 million rods and 6 million cones turn it into nerve signals for the brain.
parts.kid: Your eyes are like cameras — the pupil lets light in and the retina takes the picture.

parts.name: Iris
parts.d: The coloured ring of muscle behind the cornea. The hole in its centre is the pupil.
parts.fn: Widens or narrows the pupil to control how much light enters the eye — like the aperture of a camera.
parts.kid: The coloured part of your eye makes the black pupil bigger in the dark and smaller in bright light.

parts.name: Lens
parts.d: A transparent, flexible disc behind the iris, held in place by fine ligaments.
parts.fn: Changes shape to fine-focus near and far objects. With age it stiffens (presbyopia) and may cloud over (cataract).
parts.kid: The lens bends light so what you look at is sharp, not blurry.

parts.name: Auricle
parts.d: The visible outer ear: a curled plate of elastic cartilage covered with skin, with the fleshy earlobe at the bottom.
parts.fn: Collects sound waves and funnels them into the ear canal; its folds help you tell whether a sound comes from above, below, in front or behind.
parts.kid: Your outer ear is a sound catcher.

parts.name: Cochlea
parts.d: A snail-shaped, fluid-filled tube of 2½ turns inside the temporal bone — the organ of hearing.
parts.fn: Sound waves ripple its fluid; about 15 000 hair cells along it turn different pitches into nerve signals sent along the cochlear nerve.
parts.kid: Deep in your ear is a tiny snail shell that turns sound into signals for your brain.

parts.name: Semicircular Canals
parts.d: Three fluid-filled loops set at right angles to each other in the inner ear.
parts.fn: Sense rotation of the head in any direction, feeding the brain's sense of balance. Spinning makes the fluid keep moving afterwards — that's why you feel dizzy.
parts.kid: Three little loops in your ear tell your brain which way you're turning.

parts.name: Tympanic Membrane
parts.d: The eardrum: a thin cone-shaped membrane about 9 mm across at the end of the ear canal.
parts.fn: Vibrates with incoming sound and passes the vibrations to the malleus.
parts.kid: Sound makes your eardrum wobble like the skin of a drum.

parts.name: Upper Central Incisor
parts.d: Chisel-shaped front tooth, in the upper jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Bites and cuts food.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Lower Central Incisor
parts.d: Chisel-shaped front tooth, in the lower jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Bites and cuts food.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Upper Lateral Incisor
parts.d: Narrower cutting tooth beside the central incisor, in the upper jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Cuts food and guides the jaw when you bite.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Lower Lateral Incisor
parts.d: Narrower cutting tooth beside the central incisor, in the lower jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Cuts food and guides the jaw when you bite.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Upper Canine
parts.d: The pointed 'eye tooth' with the longest root of any tooth, in the upper jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Grips and tears food and guides the jaw sideways.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Lower Canine
parts.d: The pointed 'eye tooth' with the longest root of any tooth, in the lower jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Grips and tears food and guides the jaw sideways.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Upper First Premolar
parts.d: A two-cusped tooth behind the canine, in the upper jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Crushes and tears food.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Lower First Premolar
parts.d: A two-cusped tooth behind the canine, in the lower jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Crushes and tears food.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Upper Second Premolar
parts.d: The second two-cusped tooth, in the upper jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Crushes food before it reaches the molars.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Lower Second Premolar
parts.d: The second two-cusped tooth, in the lower jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Crushes food before it reaches the molars.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Upper First Molar
parts.d: A broad grinding tooth with four or five cusps — usually the first permanent tooth to erupt, at about 6 years, in the upper jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Grinds food; the main chewing tooth.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Lower First Molar
parts.d: A broad grinding tooth with four or five cusps — usually the first permanent tooth to erupt, at about 6 years, in the lower jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Grinds food; the main chewing tooth.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Upper Second Molar
parts.d: Grinding tooth that erupts at about 12 years, in the upper jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Grinds food.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Lower Second Molar
parts.d: Grinding tooth that erupts at about 12 years, in the lower jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Grinds food.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Upper Third Molar
parts.d: The wisdom tooth, erupting between 17 and 25 — if there is room, in the upper jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Adds grinding surface; often removed when impacted.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Lower Third Molar
parts.d: The wisdom tooth, erupting between 17 and 25 — if there is room, in the lower jaw. Each tooth has an enamel crown — the hardest substance in the body — over dentine, with a pulp of nerves and vessels in the middle.
parts.fn: Adds grinding surface; often removed when impacted.
parts.kid: Adults have 32 teeth; children have 20 baby teeth.

parts.name: Tongue
parts.d: A muscular organ covered with papillae; its surface carries 2 000–8 000 taste buds.
parts.fn: Moves food around for chewing, shapes it into a ball for swallowing, detects the five basic tastes and is essential for speech.
parts.kid: Your tongue is made of muscles and can taste sweet, salty, sour, bitter and savoury.

parts.name: Parotid Gland
parts.d: The largest salivary gland, wrapped around the back of the jaw in front of the ear. Its duct opens inside the cheek opposite the upper second molar.
parts.fn: Produces watery saliva rich in amylase, which starts digesting starch. It swells painfully in mumps.
parts.kid: When you smell tasty food, this gland makes your mouth water.

parts.name: Submandibular Gland
parts.d: A walnut-sized gland under the angle of the jaw; its duct opens under the tongue.
parts.fn: Makes about 70% of your saliva, a mix of watery and mucous secretions.
parts.kid: It makes most of your spit!

parts.name: Sublingual Gland
parts.d: The smallest major salivary gland, lying under the tongue in the floor of the mouth.
parts.fn: Secretes thick, mucous saliva that lubricates food.
parts.kid: A small gland under your tongue keeps your mouth slippery.

parts.name: Palatine Tonsil
parts.d: An almond-shaped mass of lymphoid tissue on each side of the back of the throat.
parts.fn: Samples bacteria and viruses entering through the mouth and helps train the immune system, especially in childhood.
parts.kid: Tonsils are guards at the back of your throat that catch germs.

parts.name: Adenoids
parts.d: The pharyngeal tonsil, a pad of lymphoid tissue at the back of the nasal cavity. It is largest in childhood and shrinks by adolescence.
parts.fn: Traps germs breathed in through the nose; enlarged adenoids can cause snoring and blocked ears in children.
parts.kid: Hidden behind your nose, the adenoids help fight colds.

parts.name: Nasal Cavity
parts.d: The air passage behind the nose, split in two by the septum and lined with moist, hair-covered mucous membrane. The olfactory area in its roof detects smells.
parts.fn: Warms, moistens and filters about 10 000 litres of air a day before it reaches the lungs, and gives your voice its resonance.
parts.kid: The inside of your nose warms and cleans the air you breathe.

parts.name: Pharynx
parts.d: The throat: a 12–14 cm muscular tube from the back of the nose down to the larynx and oesophagus, divided into nasopharynx, oropharynx and laryngopharynx.
parts.fn: A shared passage for air and food. When you swallow, its muscles squeeze food down while the epiglottis closes the airway.
parts.kid: Food and air share this tube at the back of your mouth.

parts.name: Epiglottis
parts.d: A leaf-shaped flap of elastic cartilage behind the root of the tongue.
parts.fn: Folds down over the entrance to the larynx every time you swallow so food goes into the oesophagus, not the windpipe.
parts.kid: A tiny trapdoor stops food going down the wrong way.

parts.name: Larynx
parts.aka: voice box adam's apple thyroid cartilage
parts.d: The voice box, built of nine cartilages joined by muscles and ligaments. The thyroid cartilage forms the Adam's apple, which grows larger in males at puberty.
parts.fn: Protects the airway, holds the vocal folds that vibrate to make sound, and closes tightly when you cough or strain.
parts.kid: Hum and touch your throat — you can feel your voice box buzzing.

meta.Cartilages: Thyroid, cricoid, epiglottis, arytenoids (×2) and others

parts.name: Vocal Fold
parts.d: Two bands of muscle and elastic ligament stretched across the larynx, about 1.5 cm long in men and 1 cm in women.
parts.fn: Snap together and vibrate as air passes to produce voice; tension and length set the pitch.
parts.kid: Your vocal cords wobble super fast to make your voice.

meta.Vibration: Around 100–250 times per second when speaking

parts.name: Trachea
parts.d: The windpipe: a tube about 11 cm long held open by 16–20 C-shaped rings of cartilage, running from the larynx to its fork (the carina) behind the sternum.
parts.fn: Conducts air to the lungs. Its lining of mucus and beating cilia sweeps dust and germs up and away from the lungs.
parts.kid: The rings in your windpipe keep it open like the hose of a vacuum cleaner.

parts.name: Thyroid Gland
parts.d: A butterfly-shaped gland of two lobes joined by an isthmus, wrapped around the front of the trachea just below the larynx.
parts.fn: Uses iodine to make the hormones T4 and T3, which set the pace of metabolism, heart rate, body temperature and growth; also makes calcitonin.
parts.kid: This butterfly-shaped gland controls how fast your body uses energy.

parts.name: Superior Parathyroid Gland
parts.d: One of four rice-grain-sized glands on the back of the thyroid.
parts.fn: Secretes parathyroid hormone (PTH), which raises blood calcium by releasing it from bone, saving it in the kidneys and activating vitamin D.
parts.kid: Four tiny glands keep the right amount of calcium in your blood.

parts.name: Inferior Parathyroid Gland
parts.d: One of four rice-grain-sized glands on the back of the thyroid.
parts.fn: Secretes parathyroid hormone (PTH), which raises blood calcium by releasing it from bone, saving it in the kidneys and activating vitamin D.
parts.kid: Four tiny glands keep the right amount of calcium in your blood.

parts.name: Left Ventricle
parts.d: The thick-walled chamber at the bottom left of the heart that forms the apex. Its wall is about three times thicker than the right ventricle's.
parts.fn: Pumps oxygen-rich blood through the aortic valve into the aorta and out to the whole body, generating the systolic blood pressure.
parts.kid: This is the strongest part of your heart — it pushes blood all the way to your toes.

meta.Output: About 5 L of blood a minute at rest

parts.name: Right Ventricle
parts.d: The crescent-shaped chamber at the front of the heart, wrapped around the left ventricle.
parts.fn: Pumps oxygen-poor blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary arteries and on to the lungs at low pressure.
parts.kid: This chamber sends used blood to your lungs to pick up fresh oxygen.

parts.name: Left Atrium
parts.d: The chamber at the back of the heart that receives blood from the four pulmonary veins. Its small ear-like pouch is the left auricle.
parts.fn: Collects oxygen-rich blood returning from the lungs and pushes it through the mitral valve into the left ventricle.
parts.kid: Fresh blood from your lungs arrives here first.

parts.name: Right Atrium
parts.d: The chamber on the right side of the heart that receives blood from the superior and inferior venae cavae and the coronary sinus. Its wall holds the heart's natural pacemaker.
parts.fn: Collects oxygen-poor blood from the body and passes it through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle.
parts.kid: Blood coming back from your body pours into this chamber.

parts.name: Mitral Valve
parts.d: The two-leaflet valve between the left atrium and left ventricle.
parts.fn: Opens to let blood into the left ventricle and snaps shut when it contracts, stopping backflow into the lungs.
parts.kid: Heart valves are one-way doors — their closing makes the 'lub-dub' sound.

parts.name: Tricuspid Valve
parts.d: The three-leaflet valve between the right atrium and right ventricle.
parts.fn: Stops blood flowing back into the right atrium when the right ventricle contracts.
parts.kid: Heart valves are one-way doors — their closing makes the 'lub-dub' sound.

parts.name: Aortic Valve
parts.d: Three half-moon cusps at the exit of the left ventricle. The coronary arteries open just above it.
parts.fn: Lets blood out into the aorta and closes to prevent it falling back into the ventricle.
parts.kid: Heart valves are one-way doors — their closing makes the 'lub-dub' sound.

parts.name: Pulmonary Valve
parts.d: Three half-moon cusps at the exit of the right ventricle.
parts.fn: Opens as the right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs, then closes to stop it flowing back.
parts.kid: Heart valves are one-way doors — their closing makes the 'lub-dub' sound.

parts.name: Sinoatrial Node
parts.d: A small patch of specialised muscle cells in the wall of the right atrium where the superior vena cava enters.
parts.fn: The heart's natural pacemaker: it fires an electrical impulse 60–100 times a minute that starts every heartbeat.
parts.kid: A tiny spark-maker in your heart starts every heartbeat.

parts.name: Atrioventricular Node
parts.d: A cluster of conducting cells in the wall between the atria, just above the tricuspid valve.
parts.fn: Delays each impulse by about a tenth of a second so the atria finish emptying, then passes it down the bundle of His to the ventricles.
parts.kid: It makes the top of the heart squeeze just before the bottom.

parts.name: Right Upper Lobe
parts.d: The top lobe of the right lung, above the horizontal fissure. Its apex rises about 2–3 cm above the collarbone.
parts.fn: Swaps gases with the blood: oxygen passes from the air in about 300 million alveoli into the capillaries, and carbon dioxide passes out to be breathed away.
parts.kid: Your right lung has three parts and your left lung has two — to make room for your heart.

parts.name: Right Middle Lobe
parts.d: The small wedge-shaped middle lobe found only in the right lung, between the horizontal and oblique fissures.
parts.fn: Swaps gases with the blood: oxygen passes from the air in about 300 million alveoli into the capillaries, and carbon dioxide passes out to be breathed away.
parts.kid: Only your right lung has a middle part.

parts.name: Right Lower Lobe
parts.d: The largest lobe of the right lung, below the oblique fissure, resting on the dome of the diaphragm.
parts.fn: Swaps gases with the blood: oxygen passes from the air in about 300 million alveoli into the capillaries, and carbon dioxide passes out to be breathed away.
parts.kid: The bottom of your lungs sits on a big breathing muscle called the diaphragm.

meta.Segments: Five basal segments plus the superior segment

parts.name: Left Upper Lobe
parts.d: The upper lobe of the left lung. Its lower front part, the lingula, curls round the cardiac notch where the heart sits.
parts.fn: Swaps gases with the blood: oxygen passes from the air in about 300 million alveoli into the capillaries, and carbon dioxide passes out to be breathed away.
parts.kid: Your left lung is a bit smaller than your right to leave room for your heart.

meta.Segments: Apicoposterior, anterior, superior and inferior lingular

parts.name: Left Lower Lobe
parts.d: The lower lobe of the left lung, below and behind the oblique fissure.
parts.fn: Swaps gases with the blood: oxygen passes from the air in about 300 million alveoli into the capillaries, and carbon dioxide passes out to be breathed away.
parts.kid: Deep breaths fill the bottom of your lungs.

parts.name: Right Main Bronchus
parts.d: The wider, shorter and more vertical of the two main bronchi — which is why inhaled objects usually lodge in the right lung.
parts.fn: Carries air from the trachea into the lung, where it divides into lobar bronchi.
parts.kid: The windpipe splits into two tubes, one for each lung.

parts.name: Right Bronchial Tree
parts.d: The branching airways inside the lung: lobar, segmental and ever smaller bronchi, then bronchioles — about 23 generations of branching in all.
parts.fn: Distributes air evenly to the alveoli. Smooth muscle in the smaller airways tightens during an asthma attack.
parts.kid: Inside your lungs the airways branch like an upside-down tree.

parts.name: Left Main Bronchus
parts.d: The narrower, longer main bronchus, which passes under the aortic arch to reach the left lung.
parts.fn: Carries air from the trachea into the lung, where it divides into lobar bronchi.
parts.kid: The windpipe splits into two tubes, one for each lung.

parts.name: Left Bronchial Tree
parts.d: The branching airways inside the lung: lobar, segmental and ever smaller bronchi, then bronchioles — about 23 generations of branching in all.
parts.fn: Distributes air evenly to the alveoli. Smooth muscle in the smaller airways tightens during an asthma attack.
parts.kid: Inside your lungs the airways branch like an upside-down tree.

parts.name: Diaphragm
parts.d: A dome-shaped sheet of muscle and tendon separating the chest from the abdomen. The aorta, oesophagus and inferior vena cava pass through it.
parts.fn: The main muscle of breathing: it contracts and flattens to draw air into the lungs, and relaxes to let it out. It also helps with coughing, vomiting and pushing during childbirth.
parts.kid: When this muscle moves down, air rushes into your lungs. Hiccups are little spasms of the diaphragm!

parts.name: Oesophagus
parts.d: The food pipe: a 25 cm muscular tube from the throat, behind the trachea and heart, through the diaphragm to the stomach.
parts.fn: Moves swallowed food to the stomach with waves of muscle contraction (peristalsis) — it works even upside down. A ring of muscle at the bottom stops acid coming back up.
parts.kid: Food doesn't just fall down this tube — muscles squeeze it along, even if you're upside down.

parts.name: Stomach
parts.d: A J-shaped muscular bag in the upper left abdomen, below the diaphragm. Its regions are the cardia, fundus, body, antrum and pylorus.
parts.fn: Stores a meal, churns it with hydrochloric acid and pepsin into a paste called chyme, and releases it little by little into the duodenum. It also makes intrinsic factor, needed to absorb vitamin B12.
parts.kid: Your stomach is a stretchy bag that mashes food with strong acid.

parts.name: Duodenum
parts.d: The first 25 cm of the small intestine, a C-shaped loop wrapped around the head of the pancreas.
parts.fn: Receives chyme from the stomach plus bile and pancreatic juice, which neutralise the acid and break down fats, proteins and carbohydrates.
parts.kid: Digestive juices from the liver and pancreas squirt into this part.

parts.name: Jejunum
parts.d: The middle section of the small intestine, about 2.5 m long, lying mostly in the upper left abdomen. Its thick, velvety lining is folded into finger-like villi.
parts.fn: Absorbs most of the sugars, amino acids and fatty acids released by digestion.
parts.kid: If you stretched out your small intestine it would be longer than a car!

parts.name: Ileum
parts.d: The final and longest section of the small intestine (about 3.5 m), in the lower right abdomen, ending at the ileocaecal valve.
parts.fn: Absorbs vitamin B12 and bile salts and whatever nutrients the jejunum missed; its Peyer's patches are an important part of gut immunity.
parts.kid: The last part of the small intestine soaks up vitamin B12.

parts.name: Caecum
parts.d: A pouch about 6 cm long at the start of the large intestine, in the lower right abdomen, where the ileum joins.
parts.fn: Receives liquid waste from the small intestine and starts absorbing water and salts.
parts.kid: The large intestine starts with a little pouch.

parts.name: Appendix
parts.d: A narrow, finger-like tube 5–10 cm long hanging from the caecum.
parts.fn: Contains lymphoid tissue and may act as a safe store of friendly gut bacteria. When it becomes blocked and inflamed (appendicitis) it usually has to be removed.
parts.kid: The appendix is a tiny tube that sometimes has to be taken out if it gets sore.

parts.name: Ascending Colon
parts.d: The part of the colon rising up the right side of the abdomen from the caecum to the hepatic flexure under the liver.
parts.fn: Absorbs water and salts from liquid waste.
parts.kid: The large intestine takes water back out of leftover food.

parts.name: Transverse Colon
parts.d: The longest and most mobile part of the colon, hanging across the abdomen between the liver and spleen.
parts.fn: Continues absorbing water; its gut bacteria ferment fibre and make vitamin K.
parts.kid: The large intestine takes water back out of leftover food.

parts.name: Descending Colon
parts.d: The part of the colon running down the left side of the abdomen from the splenic flexure.
parts.fn: Stores faeces that are becoming solid on their way to the rectum.
parts.kid: The large intestine takes water back out of leftover food.

parts.name: Sigmoid Colon
parts.d: An S-shaped loop of colon in the lower left pelvis, joining the descending colon to the rectum.
parts.fn: Holds faeces until they are ready to pass into the rectum.
parts.kid: The large intestine takes water back out of leftover food.

parts.name: Rectum
parts.d: The last 12 cm of the large intestine, following the curve of the sacrum.
parts.fn: Stores faeces until you go to the toilet; stretch receptors in its wall create the urge to go.
parts.kid: This is the waiting room before poo leaves your body.

parts.name: Anal Canal
parts.d: The final 3–4 cm of the digestive tract, surrounded by internal and external sphincter muscles.
parts.fn: Keeps faeces in and gas under control until you choose to let them out.
parts.kid: Two rings of muscle keep it closed until you're on the toilet.

parts.name: Liver — Right Lobe
parts.d: The larger of the liver's two lobes, filling the upper right abdomen under the ribs. The liver is the body's largest internal organ, weighing about 1.5 kg.
parts.fn: Processes everything absorbed from the gut, stores glycogen, vitamins and iron, makes bile, blood proteins such as albumin and clotting factors, and breaks down alcohol, drugs and old red cells.
parts.kid: Your liver does over 500 jobs, like cleaning your blood — and it can regrow if part is removed!

parts.name: Liver — Left Lobe
parts.d: The smaller, flatter lobe of the liver, extending to the left over the stomach, separated from the right lobe by the falciform ligament.
parts.fn: Shares all of the liver's metabolic, storage and detoxifying work.
parts.kid: The liver's left side is smaller and sits over your stomach.

parts.name: Gallbladder
parts.d: A pear-shaped sac about 8 cm long tucked under the right lobe of the liver.
parts.fn: Stores and concentrates bile and squeezes it into the duodenum after a fatty meal. Hardened bile forms gallstones.
parts.kid: It squirts green bile to help you digest fatty food.

parts.name: Bile Ducts
parts.aka: common bile duct hepatic duct cystic duct
parts.d: The hepatic, cystic and common bile ducts: the plumbing that carries bile from the liver and gallbladder to the duodenum.
parts.fn: Deliver bile to the gut. A stone or tumour blocking them causes jaundice.
parts.kid: Tiny tubes carry bile from your liver to your gut.

meta.Opens: Major duodenal papilla, with the pancreatic duct

parts.name: Pancreas
parts.d: A soft, 15 cm long gland lying behind the stomach, with its head in the curve of the duodenum and its tail touching the spleen.
parts.fn: Two jobs in one: it pours about 1.5 litres of digestive enzymes a day into the duodenum, and its islets of Langerhans release insulin and glucagon to control blood sugar.
parts.kid: The pancreas makes insulin, which lets sugar from your food get into your cells.

parts.name: Spleen
parts.d: A fist-sized organ in the upper left abdomen, tucked under ribs 9–11 behind the stomach.
parts.fn: Filters the blood, removing old and damaged red cells, recycles their iron, stores platelets and white cells, and fights blood-borne infections.
parts.kid: Your spleen is a blood filter that also helps fight germs.

parts.name: Kidney
parts.d: A bean-shaped organ about 11 cm long against the back wall of the abdomen, at the level of T12–L3. The right kidney sits a little lower than the left because of the liver.
parts.fn: Filters about 180 litres of blood plasma a day through a million nephrons each, keeping water, salts, acid and blood pressure in balance and producing 1–2 litres of urine. Also makes erythropoietin (EPO) and activates vitamin D.
parts.kid: Your kidneys clean your blood and turn the waste into pee.

parts.name: Ureter
parts.d: A muscular tube 25–30 cm long carrying urine from each kidney down to the bladder.
parts.fn: Pushes urine downward with waves of contraction; kidney stones cause intense pain when they get stuck in it.
parts.kid: Two thin tubes carry pee from your kidneys to your bladder.

parts.name: Urinary Bladder
parts.d: A hollow, stretchy muscular bag in the pelvis behind the pubic bone.
parts.fn: Stores urine and empties it through the urethra when you choose to go.
parts.kid: Your bladder is like a balloon that fills with pee and tells you when it's time to go.

parts.name: Urethra
parts.d: In males, a tube about 20 cm long running from the bladder through the prostate and penis.
parts.fn: Carries urine out of the body, and in males also carries semen.
parts.kid: Pee leaves your body through this tube.

parts.name: Urethra
parts.d: In females, a short tube about 4 cm long from the bladder to the outside, in front of the vagina.
parts.fn: Carries urine out of the body. Its shortness is why urinary infections are more common in women.
parts.kid: Pee leaves your body through this tube.

parts.name: Adrenal Gland
parts.d: A small triangular gland capping the top of each kidney, made of an outer cortex and inner medulla.
parts.fn: The cortex makes cortisol (stress and blood sugar), aldosterone (salt and blood pressure) and androgens; the medulla releases adrenaline and noradrenaline for fight or flight.
parts.kid: When you're scared, these glands pump out adrenaline so you can run fast.

parts.name: Thymus
parts.d: A two-lobed organ behind the top of the sternum. It is largest at puberty and is gradually replaced by fat in adults.
parts.fn: Where T-lymphocytes mature and learn to tell the body's own cells from invaders.
parts.kid: The thymus is a school where your germ-fighting T-cells learn their job.

parts.name: Thoracic Duct
parts.d: The largest lymph vessel, about 40 cm long, running up in front of the spine from the cisterna chyli to the junction of the left subclavian and internal jugular veins.
parts.fn: Returns about three-quarters of the body's lymph — plus fats absorbed from the gut — to the bloodstream.
parts.kid: This long tube returns lymph fluid to your blood.

parts.name: Cisterna Chyli
parts.d: A sac at the bottom of the thoracic duct in front of L1–L2.
parts.fn: Collects milky, fat-rich lymph (chyle) from the intestines and lymph from the legs.
parts.kid: A little collecting bag for lymph from your belly.

parts.name: Cervical Lymph Nodes
parts.d: Chains of lymph nodes along the internal jugular vein and under the jaw.
parts.fn: Filter lymph from the head and neck — the lumps you can feel under your jaw during a sore throat.
parts.kid: Lymph nodes are like filters that trap germs. They swell up when you're sick.

parts.name: Axillary Lymph Nodes
parts.d: 20–40 lymph nodes in the fat of the armpit.
parts.fn: Filter lymph from the arm and chest wall, including the breast — which is why they are checked in breast cancer.
parts.kid: Lymph nodes are like filters that trap germs. They swell up when you're sick.

parts.name: Inguinal Lymph Nodes
parts.d: Lymph nodes in the groin, below the inguinal ligament.
parts.fn: Filter lymph from the leg, buttock and lower abdominal wall.
parts.kid: Lymph nodes are like filters that trap germs. They swell up when you're sick.

parts.name: Mesenteric Lymph Nodes
parts.d: Hundreds of nodes in the mesentery, the fan of tissue that holds the intestines.
parts.fn: Filter lymph and absorbed fat coming from the gut and start immune responses to gut infections.
parts.kid: Lymph nodes are like filters that trap germs. They swell up when you're sick.

parts.name: Mediastinal Lymph Nodes
parts.d: Lymph nodes in the centre of the chest around the trachea and bronchi.
parts.fn: Drain the lungs and heart; they can be blackened by soot in city dwellers and smokers.
parts.kid: Lymph nodes are like filters that trap germs. They swell up when you're sick.

parts.name: Para-aortic Lymph Nodes
parts.d: Lymph nodes along the abdominal aorta.
parts.fn: Drain the kidneys, adrenals and gonads — testicular and ovarian cancers spread here first.
parts.kid: Lymph nodes are like filters that trap germs. They swell up when you're sick.

parts.name: Testis
parts.d: An oval gland about 4–5 cm long held in the scrotum, outside the body where it is 2–3 °C cooler.
parts.fn: Produces sperm (about 100 million a day) and the hormone testosterone.
parts.kid: The testes make the cells that can grow into a baby.

parts.name: Epididymis
parts.d: A tightly coiled tube about 6 metres long packed along the back of each testis.
parts.fn: Stores sperm while they mature and learn to swim.
parts.kid: A long coiled tube where sperm grow up.

parts.name: Vas Deferens
parts.d: A muscular tube about 45 cm long that runs from the epididymis up through the groin, over the ureter and behind the bladder to the prostate.
parts.fn: Propels sperm towards the urethra during ejaculation. Cutting it (vasectomy) is a permanent form of contraception.
parts.kid: A tube that carries sperm from the testes.

parts.name: Seminal Vesicle
parts.d: A coiled gland about 5 cm long behind the bladder.
parts.fn: Makes about 70% of the fluid in semen, rich in fructose that fuels the sperm.
parts.kid: It makes the fluid that carries sperm.

parts.name: Prostate
parts.d: A walnut-sized gland below the bladder that surrounds the first part of the urethra.
parts.fn: Adds a milky, alkaline fluid to semen. It commonly enlarges with age, making urination slower; PSA is the blood test used to monitor it.
parts.kid: A gland just under the bladder, found only in boys and men.

parts.name: Penis
parts.d: The external male organ, made of three columns of spongy erectile tissue around the urethra.
parts.fn: Carries urine and semen out of the body through the urethra.
parts.kid: Boys pee through their penis.

parts.name: Scrotum
parts.d: The pouch of skin and smooth muscle that holds the testes outside the abdomen.
parts.fn: Keeps the testes a few degrees cooler than the core, which sperm production needs, tightening in the cold and relaxing in the warm.
parts.kid: It keeps the testes cool.

parts.name: Ovary
parts.d: An almond-sized gland on each side of the uterus. At birth each ovary holds about a million immature eggs.
parts.fn: Releases an egg about once a month from puberty to menopause and makes the hormones oestrogen and progesterone.
parts.kid: Ovaries store tiny eggs that could one day grow into a baby.

parts.name: Fallopian Tube
parts.d: A slender tube about 10 cm long from the top of the uterus to the ovary, ending in finger-like fimbriae.
parts.fn: Catches the egg released by the ovary; fertilisation usually happens here, and the tube then carries the embryo to the uterus.
parts.kid: The egg travels down this tube to reach the womb.

parts.name: Uterus
parts.d: The womb: a hollow, pear-shaped muscular organ about 7.5 cm long, tilted forward over the bladder. Its lining (endometrium) thickens and sheds each menstrual cycle.
parts.fn: Nourishes and protects a developing baby for about nine months, stretching to hundreds of times its size, then contracts powerfully during birth.
parts.kid: The womb is where a baby grows before it is born.

parts.name: Vagina
parts.d: A muscular, elastic canal about 8 cm long from the cervix to the outside of the body.
parts.fn: Lets menstrual blood out, receives sperm and stretches to become the birth canal.
parts.kid: Babies are usually born through this stretchy canal.

parts.name: Mammary Gland
parts.d: Breast tissue made of 15–20 lobes of milk glands set in fat, each drained by a duct that opens at the nipple.
parts.fn: Produces milk after childbirth under the control of the hormones prolactin and oxytocin.
parts.kid: Mothers' bodies make milk here to feed their babies.

parts.name: Skin
parts.d: The body's largest organ, covering about 1.8 m² and weighing around 4 kg. It has three layers: the epidermis, the dermis and the fatty hypodermis.
parts.fn: Keeps germs out and water in, controls temperature by sweating and flushing, senses touch, pain, heat and cold, and makes vitamin D in sunlight.
parts.kid: Your skin is your biggest organ — it replaces its whole outer layer about once a month!

parts.name: Ascending Aorta
parts.d: The first 5 cm of the aorta, rising from the left ventricle behind the sternum. The two coronary arteries branch off at its root.
parts.fn: Receives every beat of the left ventricle and feeds the coronary arteries that supply the heart muscle itself.
parts.kid: The aorta is your biggest artery — about as wide as a garden hose.

parts.name: Aortic Arch
parts.d: The curve of the aorta above the heart, arching backwards and to the left over the left main bronchus. Three large arteries leave its top: the brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid and left subclavian.
parts.fn: Distributes blood to the head, neck and arms; pressure sensors in its wall help regulate blood pressure.
parts.kid: The aorta makes a U-turn over your heart like a walking cane.

meta.Branches: Brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid, left subclavian

parts.name: Brachiocephalic Trunk
parts.d: The first and largest branch of the aortic arch, about 4 cm long, found only on the right.
