parts.fn: Divides into the right common carotid artery (to the head) and right subclavian artery (to the arm).
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Thoracic Aorta
parts.d: The descending aorta in the chest, running down the left side of the vertebral bodies from T4 to the diaphragm.
parts.fn: Gives off intercostal arteries to the chest wall and branches to the oesophagus and bronchi, then passes through the diaphragm at T12.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Abdominal Aorta
parts.d: The aorta below the diaphragm, lying just in front of the lumbar spine. It divides into the two common iliac arteries at about the level of the navel (L4).
parts.fn: Supplies the gut, liver, spleen, kidneys and adrenals through its major branches. A ballooning of this segment is called an abdominal aortic aneurysm.
parts.kid: You can sometimes feel it beating if you press gently on your tummy.

parts.name: Coronary Arteries
parts.d: The left coronary artery (dividing into the left anterior descending and circumflex branches) and the right coronary artery, running in grooves on the surface of the heart.
parts.fn: Supply the heart muscle with oxygen. A clot blocking one of them causes a heart attack (myocardial infarction).
parts.kid: The heart feeds itself through its own small arteries wrapped around it like a crown.

parts.name: Pulmonary Trunk & Arteries
parts.d: The short, wide trunk leaving the right ventricle and its two branches to the lungs. They are the only arteries in the adult body that carry oxygen-poor blood.
parts.fn: Deliver blood from the right heart to the lungs to collect oxygen and unload carbon dioxide.
parts.kid: These arteries are drawn blue because they carry 'used' blood to the lungs.

parts.name: Common Carotid Artery
parts.d: The main artery of the neck, running up beside the trachea and larynx. On the left it rises from the aortic arch, on the right from the brachiocephalic trunk.
parts.fn: Carries blood towards the head. You can feel its pulse beside the windpipe; the carotid sinus at its fork senses blood pressure.
parts.kid: Put two fingers on the side of your neck — that thump is your carotid artery.

meta.Divides: Internal and external carotid, at C4

parts.name: Internal Carotid Artery
parts.d: The branch of the common carotid that enters the skull through the carotid canal without giving any branches in the neck.
parts.fn: Supplies most of the brain (with the vertebral arteries) and the eye through the ophthalmic artery.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: External Carotid Artery
parts.d: The branch of the common carotid that supplies the outside of the head, running up behind the jaw to become the superficial temporal artery at the temple.
parts.fn: Feeds the face, scalp, tongue, jaw and neck through branches such as the facial, lingual and maxillary arteries.
parts.kid: You can feel this artery's pulse at your temple.

meta.Branches: Facial, lingual, maxillary, superficial temporal, occipital

parts.name: Vertebral Artery
parts.d: Rises from the subclavian artery and climbs through holes in the cervical vertebrae, entering the skull through the foramen magnum.
parts.fn: Joins its partner to form the basilar artery, which supplies the brainstem, cerebellum and back of the brain.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Basilar Artery & Circle of Willis
parts.d: A ring of arteries under the brain that joins the two internal carotid systems with the basilar artery.
parts.fn: Provides back-up routes so that if one artery narrows, blood can reach the brain another way.
parts.kid: A ring of arteries under your brain works like a roundabout for blood.

parts.name: Subclavian Artery
parts.d: Arches over the first rib behind the collarbone. On the left it comes directly from the aortic arch; on the right from the brachiocephalic trunk.
parts.fn: Supplies the arm, and gives off the vertebral and internal thoracic arteries.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

meta.Becomes: Axillary artery at the first rib

parts.name: Axillary Artery
parts.d: Continues the subclavian artery through the armpit, surrounded by the cords of the brachial plexus.
parts.fn: Supplies the shoulder, chest wall and armpit.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Brachial Artery
parts.d: The main artery of the upper arm, running down its inner side beside the median nerve to the front of the elbow.
parts.fn: Supplies the arm; it is the artery squeezed by a blood-pressure cuff and listened to with a stethoscope.
parts.kid: When a nurse measures your blood pressure, they squeeze this artery.

meta.Divides: Radial and ulnar arteries at the elbow

parts.name: Radial Artery
parts.d: Runs down the thumb side of the forearm to the wrist, where it lies just under the skin.
parts.fn: Supplies the forearm and hand; it is where you usually feel your pulse at the wrist.
parts.kid: Feel your pulse on the thumb side of your wrist — that's the radial artery.

parts.name: Ulnar Artery
parts.d: The larger of the two forearm arteries, running down the little-finger side.
parts.fn: Supplies the forearm and most of the hand through the superficial palmar arch.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Palmar Arches
parts.d: Two arterial loops in the palm formed by the radial and ulnar arteries, giving off digital arteries along each finger.
parts.fn: Supply the hand with a double blood supply so it stays pink even if one artery is blocked.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Coeliac Trunk
parts.d: A short, wide artery from the front of the aorta just below the diaphragm that splits into the left gastric, common hepatic and splenic arteries.
parts.fn: Supplies the stomach, liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen and the first part of the duodenum.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Superior Mesenteric Artery
parts.d: Arises from the aorta just below the coeliac trunk and fans out through the mesentery.
parts.fn: Supplies the small intestine, the caecum, the ascending colon and most of the transverse colon — the midgut.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Inferior Mesenteric Artery
parts.d: The smallest of the three gut arteries, arising from the aorta at L3.
parts.fn: Supplies the left third of the transverse colon, the descending and sigmoid colon, and the upper rectum — the hindgut.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Renal Artery
parts.d: Short, wide arteries from the sides of the aorta to each kidney. The right one passes behind the inferior vena cava.
parts.fn: Deliver about a fifth of the heart's output to the kidneys to be filtered.
parts.kid: About a litre of blood flows into your kidneys every minute.

parts.name: Common Iliac Artery
parts.d: One of the two terminal branches of the aorta, about 4 cm long.
parts.fn: Divides into the internal iliac artery (pelvis) and external iliac artery (leg).
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Internal Iliac Artery
parts.d: The branch of the common iliac that dips into the pelvis.
parts.fn: Supplies the bladder, rectum, reproductive organs, buttock muscles and pelvic floor.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: External Iliac Artery
parts.d: Runs along the brim of the pelvis and under the inguinal ligament, where it becomes the femoral artery.
parts.fn: Carries blood to the leg.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

meta.Becomes: Femoral artery at the inguinal ligament

parts.name: Femoral Artery
parts.d: The main artery of the thigh. Just below the groin crease it lies close to the surface, where its pulse is easy to feel.
parts.fn: Supplies the thigh through the deep femoral artery and continues down as the popliteal artery. Doctors often use it to thread catheters up to the heart.
parts.kid: The big artery in your thigh carries blood down to your leg and foot.

parts.name: Popliteal Artery
parts.d: The deepest structure behind the knee, continuing the femoral artery.
parts.fn: Supplies the knee joint and divides into the anterior and posterior tibial arteries.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Anterior Tibial Artery
parts.d: Passes forward between the tibia and fibula and runs down the front of the leg; on the top of the foot it becomes the dorsalis pedis artery.
parts.fn: Supplies the muscles that lift the foot and toes. The dorsalis pedis pulse on top of the foot is checked in people with poor circulation.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Posterior Tibial Artery
parts.d: Runs down the back of the calf and behind the inner ankle bone into the sole, where it splits into the plantar arteries.
parts.fn: Supplies the calf muscles and the sole of the foot.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Fibular Artery
parts.d: A branch of the posterior tibial artery running close to the fibula.
parts.fn: Supplies the muscles on the outer side of the leg and the ankle.
parts.kid: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. This one is a branch of the big 'tree' that starts at the aorta.

parts.name: Superior Vena Cava
parts.d: A large vein about 7 cm long formed behind the right side of the sternum by the joining of the two brachiocephalic veins.
parts.fn: Returns blood from the head, neck, arms and chest to the right atrium.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Inferior Vena Cava
parts.d: The largest vein in the body, running up the right side of the lumbar spine and through the liver and diaphragm to the right atrium.
parts.fn: Returns all the blood from the legs, pelvis and abdomen to the heart.
parts.kid: Your biggest vein carries blood from your legs and tummy back to your heart.

parts.name: Brachiocephalic Vein
parts.d: The left and right brachiocephalic veins, formed behind each sternoclavicular joint where the internal jugular meets the subclavian vein. The left one is longer and crosses in front of the aortic branches.
parts.fn: Collect blood from the head, neck and arms and join to form the superior vena cava.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Internal Jugular Vein
parts.d: The main vein of the neck, running in the carotid sheath beside the carotid artery, from the base of the skull to behind the collarbone.
parts.fn: Drains blood from the brain, face and neck. Doctors use it to place central lines.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: External Jugular Vein
parts.d: A superficial vein crossing the sternocleidomastoid muscle; it stands out when you strain or shout.
parts.fn: Drains the scalp and face into the subclavian vein.
parts.kid: When you shout, you might see this vein bulge on your neck.

parts.name: Subclavian Vein
parts.d: Continues the axillary vein over the first rib, in front of the subclavian artery.
parts.fn: Returns blood from the arm; the thoracic duct empties lymph into the left one.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Axillary Vein
parts.d: The large vein of the armpit, formed by the basilic and brachial veins.
parts.fn: Drains the arm, armpit and upper chest wall.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Cephalic Vein
parts.d: A superficial vein running up the thumb side of the forearm and outer arm, then through the groove between the deltoid and pectoralis major.
parts.fn: Drains the lateral hand and arm into the axillary vein; a common site for drips.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Basilic Vein
parts.d: A superficial vein on the little-finger side of the forearm that dives deep halfway up the arm.
parts.fn: Drains the medial hand and forearm into the axillary vein.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Median Cubital Vein
parts.d: The short diagonal vein in the crook of the elbow linking the cephalic and basilic veins.
parts.fn: The favourite vein for taking blood samples — most of the lab tests in a blood report start here.
parts.kid: When you have a blood test, the needle usually goes into this vein at your elbow.

parts.name: Pulmonary Veins
parts.d: Four veins, two from each lung, entering the back of the left atrium. They are the only veins that carry oxygen-rich blood.
parts.fn: Return freshly oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left side of the heart.
parts.kid: These veins are red because they carry fresh, oxygen-filled blood from the lungs.

parts.name: Hepatic Portal Vein
parts.d: A vein about 8 cm long formed behind the pancreas by the splenic and superior mesenteric veins, with its branches.
parts.fn: Carries nutrient-rich blood from the gut and spleen to the liver to be processed before it reaches the rest of the body.
parts.kid: Blood from your gut goes to the liver first, to be checked and cleaned.

meta.Tributaries: Splenic, superior and inferior mesenteric veins

parts.name: Hepatic Veins
parts.d: Three short veins that drain the liver straight into the inferior vena cava just below the diaphragm.
parts.fn: Return blood that has passed through the liver to the heart.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Renal Vein
parts.d: Drains each kidney into the inferior vena cava; the left one is longer and crosses in front of the aorta.
parts.fn: Returns filtered blood from the kidneys.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Azygos Vein
parts.d: An unpaired vein running up the right side of the vertebral bodies and arching over the right lung root into the superior vena cava.
parts.fn: Drains the back of the chest wall and provides a bypass between the two venae cavae.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Common Iliac Vein
parts.d: Formed in the pelvis by the external and internal iliac veins; the two unite to form the inferior vena cava at L5.
parts.fn: Drains the leg and pelvis.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: External Iliac Vein
parts.d: Continues the femoral vein above the inguinal ligament, running along the pelvic brim.
parts.fn: Returns blood from the leg.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Femoral Vein
parts.d: The main deep vein of the thigh, lying just inside the femoral artery in the groin.
parts.fn: Returns blood from the leg. Clots here (deep vein thrombosis) can break off and travel to the lungs.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Popliteal Vein
parts.d: Runs up behind the knee alongside the popliteal artery.
parts.fn: Drains the lower leg and receives the small saphenous vein.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Great Saphenous Vein
parts.d: The longest vein in the body, running just under the skin from the inner side of the foot up the inside of the leg and thigh to the groin.
parts.fn: Drains the skin of the leg into the femoral vein. It is the vein most often affected by varicose veins and is used for heart-bypass grafts.
parts.kid: The longest vein in your body runs from your ankle to your groin.

parts.name: Small Saphenous Vein
parts.d: A superficial vein running from behind the outer ankle up the middle of the calf.
parts.fn: Drains the outer foot and back of the calf into the popliteal vein.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Coronary Sinus & Cardiac Veins
parts.d: The great cardiac vein climbs beside the LAD artery and curls round the back of the heart into the coronary sinus, which opens into the right atrium.
parts.fn: Drains used blood from the heart muscle itself.
parts.kid: Veins carry blood back to your heart. They look blue under your skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

parts.name: Trigeminal Nerve
parts.d: Cranial nerve V, the largest cranial nerve, with three divisions: ophthalmic, maxillary and mandibular.
parts.fn: Carries touch, pain and temperature from the face, eyes, teeth and mouth, and controls the chewing muscles.
parts.kid: This nerve feels everything on your face — including toothache!

parts.name: Facial Nerve
parts.d: Cranial nerve VII. It leaves the skull just behind the ear and fans out through the parotid gland into five branches across the face.
parts.fn: Moves the muscles of facial expression, carries taste from the front of the tongue and controls tears and saliva. Damage causes Bell's palsy.
parts.kid: This nerve lets you smile, frown, blink and wink.

parts.name: Vestibulocochlear Nerve
parts.d: Cranial nerve VIII, running from the inner ear to the brainstem.
parts.fn: Carries hearing signals from the cochlea and balance signals from the semicircular canals.
parts.kid: Sound and balance messages travel along this nerve.

parts.name: Vagus Nerve
parts.d: Cranial nerve X — 'the wanderer' — the longest cranial nerve, running from the brainstem down the neck beside the carotid artery into the chest and abdomen.
parts.fn: The main nerve of the parasympathetic 'rest and digest' system: it slows the heart, stimulates digestion and controls the muscles of the throat and voice box.
parts.kid: This nerve wanders all the way from your brain to your tummy and helps you feel calm.

parts.name: Hypoglossal Nerve
parts.d: Cranial nerve XII, looping under the jaw into the tongue.
parts.fn: Moves the tongue for speaking, chewing and swallowing.
parts.kid: It lets you stick your tongue out!

parts.name: Phrenic Nerve
parts.d: Arises from spinal nerves C3–C5 in the neck and runs down over the heart to the diaphragm.
parts.fn: The only motor supply to the diaphragm — 'C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive'. Irritation makes you hiccup.
parts.kid: This nerve tells your breathing muscle when to move.

parts.name: Sympathetic Trunk
parts.d: A chain of nerve ganglia running like a string of beads down each side of the spine from the skull to the coccyx.
parts.fn: Carries 'fight or flight' signals that speed the heart, widen the airways and pupils, and divert blood to the muscles.
parts.kid: When you're excited or scared, these nerves make your heart race.

parts.name: Intercostal Nerve 1
parts.d: The front branch of spinal nerve T1, running in the groove on the underside of rib 1 with the intercostal artery and vein.
parts.fn: Supplies the intercostal muscles between the ribs and the skin of the chest at this level — the band of skin affected when shingles strikes.
parts.kid: Nerves are like electrical wires carrying messages between your brain and body.

parts.name: Intercostal Nerve 2
parts.d: The front branch of spinal nerve T2, running in the groove on the underside of rib 2 with the intercostal artery and vein.
parts.fn: Supplies the intercostal muscles between the ribs and the skin of the chest at this level — the band of skin affected when shingles strikes.
parts.kid: Nerves are like electrical wires carrying messages between your brain and body.

parts.name: Intercostal Nerve 3
parts.d: The front branch of spinal nerve T3, running in the groove on the underside of rib 3 with the intercostal artery and vein.
parts.fn: Supplies the intercostal muscles between the ribs and the skin of the chest at this level — the band of skin affected when shingles strikes.
parts.kid: Nerves are like electrical wires carrying messages between your brain and body.

parts.name: Brachial Plexus
parts.d: A network formed by the front branches of spinal nerves C5–T1. Its roots, trunks, divisions and cords weave together in the neck and armpit.
parts.fn: Gives rise to every nerve of the arm and hand. Stretching the neck away from the shoulder can injure it.
parts.kid: Nerves are like electrical wires carrying messages between your brain and body.

parts.name: Musculocutaneous Nerve
parts.d: Pierces the coracobrachialis and runs between the biceps and brachialis.
parts.fn: Moves the biceps, brachialis and coracobrachialis (bending the elbow) and supplies the skin of the outer forearm.
parts.kid: Nerves are like electrical wires carrying messages between your brain and body.

parts.name: Axillary Nerve
parts.d: Wraps around the back of the neck of the humerus.
parts.fn: Supplies the deltoid and teres minor. It can be damaged when the shoulder dislocates or the humerus neck breaks.
parts.kid: Nerves are like electrical wires carrying messages between your brain and body.

parts.name: Radial Nerve
parts.d: The largest branch of the brachial plexus, spiralling around the back of the humerus in the radial groove.
parts.fn: Straightens the elbow, wrist and fingers and supplies the skin on the back of the hand. Injury causes 'wrist drop'.
parts.kid: Nerves are like electrical wires carrying messages between your brain and body.

parts.name: Median Nerve
parts.d: Runs down the middle of the arm and forearm and through the carpal tunnel at the wrist.
parts.fn: Controls most forearm flexors and the thumb muscles, and carries feeling from the thumb, index, middle and half the ring finger. Squeezing it in the carpal tunnel causes carpal tunnel syndrome.
parts.kid: Nerves are like electrical wires carrying messages between your brain and body.

parts.name: Ulnar Nerve
parts.d: Passes behind the medial epicondyle of the humerus at the elbow — the 'funny bone' — then down the little-finger side of the forearm.
parts.fn: Controls most small muscles of the hand for fine finger movements, and carries feeling from the little finger and half the ring finger.
parts.kid: Hitting your 'funny bone' is really bumping this nerve.

parts.name: Lumbar Plexus
parts.d: A network formed by spinal nerves L1–L4 inside the psoas major muscle.
parts.fn: Supplies the lower abdominal wall, groin and front and inner thigh through the femoral, obturator and genitofemoral nerves.
parts.kid: Nerves are like electrical wires carrying messages between your brain and body.

parts.name: Femoral Nerve
parts.d: The largest branch of the lumbar plexus, entering the thigh under the inguinal ligament just outside the femoral artery.
parts.fn: Straightens the knee through the quadriceps, bends the hip, and carries feeling from the front of the thigh and inner leg (via the saphenous nerve).
parts.kid: Nerves are like electrical wires carrying messages between your brain and body.

parts.name: Sciatic Nerve
parts.d: The thickest and longest nerve in the body — as wide as a thumb at its origin — running from the lower spine through the buttock and down the back of the thigh.
parts.fn: Supplies the hamstrings and, through its tibial and common fibular branches, every muscle below the knee. Pressure on its roots causes sciatica.
parts.kid: The biggest nerve in your body is as thick as your thumb.

parts.name: Tibial Nerve
parts.d: The larger branch of the sciatic nerve, running straight down the back of the leg and behind the inner ankle into the sole.
parts.fn: Points the foot and toes down (the push-off in walking) and carries feeling from the sole.
parts.kid: Nerves are like electrical wires carrying messages between your brain and body.

parts.name: Common Fibular Nerve
parts.d: Winds round the neck of the fibula just below the knee, where it is easily injured, then divides into deep and superficial branches.
parts.fn: Lifts the foot and toes and turns the foot outwards; damage causes 'foot drop'.
